ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (Samoa), as amended by Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (Amendment) Act 2015 and (Amendment) Act 2019, sections 4-20 and 48A; International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa) as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2018 and the International Companies (Beneficial Ownership Register) Regulations 2018.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Registered Agent / Samoan Notary Public

UBO Disclosure Statement and Ownership Chart

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening against the Samoa FIU consolidated list, UN Security Council sanctions, OFAC SDN list, EU consolidated list, and Samoa domestic sanctions list. PEPs, family members and close associates are subject to enhanced due diligence, risk rating, and continued transaction monitoring. The licensed registered agent must certify completion of such screening before incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: MCIL Companies Online Registry / Samoa International Companies Registry Portal (https://registry.mcil.gov.ws)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory corporate names must be expressed in Latin script (English or Samoan); non-Latin script names, including Chinese characters, may be used only as an embellished/parallel name after the Latin statutory name is registered; statutory name must be distinct from existing names on the Register and must not mislead or suggest government or professional sponsorship.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 21 business days of a name rejection, the applicant may file a written appeal with the Registrar of International Companies, together with a statutory declaration and a non-refundable appeal fee of US$50; the Registrar shall decide within 15 business days; if still adverse, the applicant may refer the matter for ministerial review through the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour within a further 10 business days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted as a substitute for the statutory physical registered office. The International Company must maintain a physical Samoan registered office through a licensed registered agent capable of receiving service of process. For the no-code website builder industry, remote operational headquarters are acceptable, but the registered office cannot be a mere virtual, mail-forwarding address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (10% likelihood within the first 12 months for a Standard Low-Risk no-code SaaS entity); however, unannounced on-site compliance inspections by the Registrar or the Financial Intelligence Unit remain permitted at any time.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2008; ss. 5-12 (incorporation procedure), s. 6 (registered agent), s. 29 (registered office), s. 44 (board of directors); Memorandum and Articles of Association filed under Schedule 1.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Corporate Registry Division, Apia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 - Application for Incorporation of an International Company, filed together with the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum issued or paid-up capital; the Company must have at least one member and may issue shares with or without par value. There is no escrow account requirement for an International Company, and capital may be subscribed in cash, assets, or as partly-paid shares; shares are ratified by the first board resolution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: 1. The registered office of the Company shall be situated at the address of the Company's licensed registered agent in Apia, Samoa, and the agent is approved as custodian of the statutory records. 2. The subscription for [___] Ordinary Shares of [___] each by the founding subscriber, as recorded in the register of members, be and is hereby ratified and accepted. 3. [Name] and [Name] be and are hereby appointed as first directors, and [Name] as initial Company Secretary, each to hold office until the first annual general meeting. 4. Any one director be empowered to execute banking instructions and company contracts, and the directors are authorized to adopt the common seal, arrange indemnity insurance, and file all statutory returns.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Name Reservation and Licensed Agent Engagement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) through a SIFA-licensed International Company Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a SIFA-licensed registered agent in Apia. Submit the proposed company name, ending in 'Limited' or 'Ltd', through the agent to SIFA for reservation and clearance. Ensure the name does not conflict with the Companies Act 2001 registered names, the International Companies Act 1987 register, or restricted words. Obtain the agent's formal consent to act as registered agent and custodian of statutory records.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation of the licensed agent
Proposed company name and corporate structure summary
Passport copies and proof of residential address of each founding shareholder
Bank and professional references supporting the beneficial owner know-your-customer (KYC) clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused or conflicts with an existing registration, the agent immediately files a substitute reservation citing up to two alternative names; SIFA processes the revised reservation within one business day without additional state filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) Corporate Registry through the Licensed Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The agent drafts the Memorandum and Articles of Association (M&A) conforming to Schedule 1 of the International Companies Act 1987. The founding subscriber executes the M&A together with the initial written consent of each director and the company secretary; share subscription is recorded in the register of members. Documents are executed in English; notarization is not required unless foreign legal evidence is requested by a downstream bank.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Share subscription agreement or share application form
Consent and appointment forms of each director and the company secretary
Limited power of attorney to the registered agent, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SIFA returns the M&A for correction due to defective clauses or missing consents, the agent files amendment pages and resubmits the corrected instrument; a pre-incorporation amendment is processed without penalty within two business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Corporate Registry Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form 1 (Application for Incorporation of an International Company) together with the executed M&A, the location of the proposed registered office in Apia, details of the licensed registered agent, and declarations of compliance. The application must be signed by the registered agent or a founding director and may be filed electronically through the SIFA portal or physically at the SIFA office in Apia.
required_dossiers: Form 1 duly signed by the agent or founding director
Certified copy of the Memorandum and Articles of Association
Statement of the registered office location in Samoa
Consent of the licensed registered agent to hold statutory records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a query is raised, the agent files a written response with a cover letter and any corrective documentation within 14 days of SIFA's statutory requisition; once the requisition is answered, the incorporation application proceeds without restarting the filing timeline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Government Incorporation Fee and First Annual License Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) Treasury and Ministry of Revenue
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pay the USD 300 government incorporation fee and the first-year annual license fee through the licensed agent's client trust account or by direct wire transfer to SIFA's designated account, quoting the SIFA application reference. The payment receipt is countersigned by SIFA and attached to the incorporation file. No ad valorem capital duty or stamp duty applies to an International Company's share capital.
required_dossiers: SIFA fee schedule or invoice
Bank transfer or SWIFT payment confirmation referencing the application number
SIFA application reference number
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If payment is misallocated or short-paid, the agent reconciles the remittance with SIFA Treasury using the SWIFT reference and, where necessary, issues a supplementary payment order which is cleared within one business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) - Registrar of International Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon satisfaction of all statutory requirements and receipt of the full government fees, the Registrar registers the company on the International Companies register and issues the Certificate of Incorporation bearing the company number, registered name, and date of incorporation. The agent retrieves the certificate and the certified M&A copy and compiles the corporate records book with share certificates and registers.
required_dossiers: Approved Form 1 and Memorandum and Articles of Association file
Government fee payment receipt issued by SIFA Treasury
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation contains typographical errors in the company name or date, the agent files a formal certificate correction request under Section 11 of the International Companies Act 1987; the corrected certificate is issued within three business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Governance and Initial Statutory Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Registered Agent and the newly constituted Board of Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or adopt a written circulating resolution to approve the minutes book, ratify the issue of shares, confirm the registered office and agent custody arrangement, elect officers, and, where necessary, appoint an auditor. Deliver a certified copy of the board resolution to the registered agent for the statutory records body, and obtain an independent tax opinion confirming the International Company's offshore tax-exempt treatment of non-Samoa-source digital software revenue.
required_dossiers: Signed first board resolution and meeting minutes
Register of members, directors, and company secretary
Share certificates issued to the founding subscriber
Acknowledgment of statutory record custody by the licensed agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If annual license or statutory record compliance is queried by SIFA during the first year, the agent files remedial declarations and any outstanding annual duty is paid without loss of good standing; reinstatement is completed within five business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) retains general administrative oversight, but no industrial or manufacturing license is required for an International Company that exclusively delivers cloud-based software and no-code web development services under ISIC 6201.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required - no manufacturing, trade, or domestic services operating permit is triggered by an International Company's offshore digital service activity under the International Companies Act 1987; domestic business licensing under the Business Licenses Act 2008 applies only to onshore commercial operations in Samoa.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - the activity is a virtual, cloud-delivered software and web-application builder with no physical construction, fixed installation, or discharge source and is therefore outside the EIA registration requirements of the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004 and the Environment Act 1989.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable - no point-source wastewater, atmospheric emission, or hazardous waste stream is generated by a remote software service. If a physical server room or office is established in Samoa at a future date, SEPA would require environmental notification and adherence to the Water Resources Management Act 2008 (zero non-compliant discharge) and the Waste Management Act 2011 (licensed waste handling); until then, no discharge thresholds apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not triggered - the Company has no physical workplace in Samoa beyond the licensed registered agent's premises. If the Company later leases local office space, the Occupational Safety and Health Division of MCIL requires fire safety certification, structural clearance from the Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA), and workplace registration under the Accident Compensation Corporation Act 2008.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue of the Independent State of Samoa (MfR) — official government tax administration; online taxpayer portal: https://www.revenue.gov.ws and https://tafao.revenue.gov.ws (Revenue Online Services)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Samoa International Company (IC) incorporated under the International Companies Act 1987 must first obtain a Certificate of Incorporation from the Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour. For national tax identity, the IC must then submit the prescribed TIN Registration Application (Form TIN-01) to the Ministry for Revenue, attaching the certificate of incorporation, registered office consent, certified copy of the charter, and director/shareholder identification. Non-resident entities may file the application through a licensed registered agent (registered office provider) in Apia. The Ministry for Revenue issues the Tax Identification Number (TIN) upon verification; an International Company may simultaneously file the Application for Tax Exemption Confirmation to obtain a formal certificate confirming exemption from Samoa income tax, VAGST and withholding tax on foreign-source offshore activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election is available under Samoan law. The Income Tax Act 2014 and the International Companies Act 1987 provide an automatic territorial exemption regime for International Companies: a Samoa IC is exempt from Samoa income tax, VAGST and stamp duty on all income, assets, transactions and activities conducted beyond Samoa (offshore). The IC may electively apply to the Ministry for Revenue for a written Tax Exemption Certificate to evidence its exempt status to foreign banking and payment intermediaries; no hybrid mismatch, US check-the-box, or entity re-classification election exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST) under the Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 2007 (No. 15 of 2007)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 30,000 (SAT 30,000) of taxable supplies in the preceding 12 months; a person making supplies below the threshold may voluntarily register; non-resident suppliers of imported digital services to Samoan consumers are subject to the VAGST and must register at any level once their supplies to Samoa exceed nil threshold under the reverse-charge/imported-services rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time electronic invoicing, continuous transaction control (CTC) clearance, fiscal API, or digital stamping regime is currently in force for Samoa. Taxpayers must issue compliant tax invoices (within 28 days of supply) and retain electronic records; VAGST returns are filed electronically or on paper with the Ministry for Revenue, and the Ministry conducts risk-based post-clearance audits rather than pre-clearance invoice certification.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under the VAGST Act 2007 for (i) goods physically exported from Samoa within 60 days of supply and evidenced by customs documentation; and (ii) services supplied to a non-resident who is outside Samoa at the time of supply and where the services are not performed in connection with land or goods situated in Samoa and are not used in Samoa. A Samoa International Company providing no-code website builder / SaaS services to foreign customers may zero-rate the export of those services where the recipient belongs in a foreign country and the supply is not directly used in Samoa. Offshore service income of an IC remains exempt from Samoan income tax; input VAT credits and refunds may be claimed for VAT incurred on local purchases attributable exclusively to exported supplies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (lodged electronically with the Samoa Customs Service and duly assessed/accepted, with customs acknowledgment)
Ocean Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical movement from Samoa
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or original bank credit advice showing receipt of foreign exchange proceeds from the overseas buyer
Commercial invoice, purchase order or service contract, and for services a statement of use outside Samoa
Certificate of Origin (if required by destination country, for goods exports)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Commissioner for Revenue has broad audit and reassessment powers. Zero-rated export claims that fail audit substantiation are clawed back with VAGST assessed at the standard rate of 15% plus interest from the date the refund was paid. Fraudulent export zero-rating or refund claims constitute tax evasion under the Tax Administration Act 2012 and the VAGST Act 2007, attracting penalties of up to 150% of the tax evaded, additional fines up to WST 100,000 per indictment, imprisonment for up to 7 years, and cancellation of the IC tax-exempt status. Directors and registered agents are jointly and severally liable where the IC fails to maintain proper export records.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), which administers exchange control under the Exchange Control Ordinance 1978 and supervises all licensed commercial banks in Samoa as authorised dealers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoa Tala (WST) is convertible on the current account for trade in goods and services, remittances of profits, dividends, interest, and intra-group contract payments, all routed through authorised dealers. Capital-account transactions are comparatively restricted and require case-by-case Central Bank of Samoa approval. The WS_IC, being an International Company with a 100% offshore revenue model and no Samoan source of income, is permitted to hold foreign-currency (USD, EUR, CNH, AUD) accounts and to remit profits and capital to non-resident shareholders without forced conversion into WST. Convertibility hurdles arise only where the IC books local Samoan revenue or receives cash directly in Samoa without a documented underlying software subscription contract, in which case CBS/FIU attribution scrutiny and WST conversion requirements could apply.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For resident exporters, the Exchange Control regime requires export proceeds to be collected within 180 days from the date of shipment and surrendered to an authorised dealer for conversion into Samoa Tala at the prevailing market rate. Licensed multi-currency retention accounts may be approved by the Central Bank of Samoa for exporters with recurring offshore receipts. For the WS_IC operating as a no-code website builder and SaaS platform, export receipts constitute offshore-source service income derived through Stripe and Paddle; the Central Bank of Samoa does not impose a mandatory surrender ratio (0% conversion obligation) where the funds are credited to an approved foreign-currency account of an International Company and supported by invoice and merchant settlement evidence for cross-border digital services, provided intra-group remittances and retained balances remain traceable for AML/CFT purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (BSP) Samoa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Foreign-Currency Account with Payment Clearing

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI providers are neither licensed nor supervised by the Central Bank of Samoa; consequently, the WS_IC cannot use an unregulated EMI as a registered bank of record for CBS reporting. Feasibility is conditionally viable: Wise, Airwallex, and similar regulated EMI/PSP rails may be used in parallel for Stripe/Paddle payout aggregation and foreign contractor disbursements, provided the EMI is properly licensed in an FATF-compliant jurisdiction and all underlying commercial documentation is mirrored to the Samoan bank. Legal constraint: the Samoa FIU and the sponsoring bank will treat the EMI as a third-party payment intermediary only, never as a substitute for an in-Samoa corporate account, and the IC must ensure that EMI activities do not create an unintended Samoa tax-residency or money-services-business exposure.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is the default requirement for directors, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorised signatories at all Samoa licensed banks. Remote video interviews may be accepted by ANZ Samoa and BSP Samoa on a case-by-case basis where the registered agent in Apia sponsors the account and physically lodges notarised passports, certified board resolutions, corporate extracts, and incumbency certificates. A physical in-country interview is in practice mandatory for directors holding 10% or more of the issued shares, for any signatory of Samoan nationality, and where the UBO resides in a high-risk or sanctions-monitored jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque offshore ownership chain without clear beneficial-owner trail
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified certificate of incorporation and incumbency for the WS_IC; notarised UBO declaration covering every natural person above 10%; updated corporate registry extract from the Samoa Registrar of International Companies; source-of-wealth report for each shareholder; a visual chain-of-title map including intermediate holding entities; bank references from the investing shareholder's originating bank; and FATCA/CRS status confirmation proving the IC is not a passive entity concealing reportable persons.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency between the declared no-code website builder scope and actual transaction flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sealed board resolution describing the product as a visual web template and low-code application builder; live domain registration and product screenshots; commercial agreement with Stripe Billing and Paddle as merchants of record; one full month of aggregated SaaS revenue report with anonymised customer invoices; cloud hosting and infrastructure supplier agreements (e.g., AWS, Google Cloud); and the company's data privacy policy confirming no prohibited local business activity in Samoa.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected high cross-border receipt and disbursement velocity, including contractor payments
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: AML/CFT risk questionnaire completed by the compliance officer and registered agent; sanctions and adverse-media screening results for all material counterparties; documented payment policy separating software vendors, overseas contractors, and shareholder distributions; invoice and contact-log library corresponding to each incoming SWIFT/Stripe settlement and outgoing MT103; board-approved transaction-volume forecast for the first 12 months; and confirmation that all underlying IP and source code are held outside Samoa and freely licenseable across borders.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder capital is injected via SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's own account at a reputable bank and credited to the WS_IC's USD operational account at ANZ Bank Samoa Limited. The remittance instruction must state the IC registration number and a descriptive purpose such as 'Equity Contribution — Subscription to Shares' with SWIFT purpose category SUBS; the receiving bank maps the credit to the Central Bank of Samoa exchange-control category for offshore equity capital. Verification documents include the certified board resolution authorising the share issuance, a shareholder subscription agreement, recent account statements evidencing source of funds, and a confirmation from the Samoa registered agent that no minimum paid-in capital requirement applies to the International Company. There is no CBS pre-approval for inbound foreign-currency equity where the funded entity is an International Company and the credit remains in a foreign-currency account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade and operating disbursements settle primarily by SWIFT MT103 for software licences, cloud infrastructure, contractor payroll, and distributor commissions. High-value procurement requiring documentary protection may use an unconfirmed or confirmed commercial letter of credit issued by ANZ Samoa or BSP Samoa against hardware, white-label subscription inventory, or aggregated software reseller purchases. Incoming producer payments from Stripe and Paddle are received via merchant network settlement into the WS_IC's foreign-currency account, then net-settled onward to suppliers through the same account, thereby avoiding unnecessary WST conversion and minimising FX drag. Every outward payment must be accompanied by a board-approved disbursement instruction, a matching invoice, and a central record retained electronically for FIU and prospective bank review.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot foreign-exchange contracts with an authorised dealer (ANZ Samoa/BSP) for limited operational conversion between USD, WST, EUR, AUD, and CNH where payment obligations are actually denominated in WST or other operating currencies.

Forward foreign-exchange contracts (standard 1-6 month tenors) executed with the Samoa authorised dealer or a bank-approved overseas correspondent to fix USD/WST, USD/AUD, and USD/EUR rates for known subscription, tax, and infrastructure disbursements.

Cross-currency swaps (plain vanilla) between USD and WST under ISDA documentation with an authorised dealer for smoothing or rebalancing of contractual cash flows, subject to CBS-style authorised-dealer reporting and prohibition of speculative net exposure.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on WST/USD booked through a Hong Kong or Singapore bank only when the Samoa authorised dealer cannot quote a deliverable tenor; the NDF must be supported by board resolution, a non-speculative hedging memo, and a corresponding cash-flow schedule of the IC's Samoan-currency obligations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of an International Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days after the anniversary of the date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of up to USD 250; continued default may result in application for administrative strike-off by the Registrar.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Government Renewal Fee / License Fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the anniversary of incorporation; a 60-day grace period applies in some cases
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late penalty per month or part of a month; non-payment for 6 months may lead to automatic dissolution and strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent Annual Compliance Confirmation and Register Update Certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Agent (licensed by Samoa International Companies Registry); no direct public filing to the Registrar unless changes occurred
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least on each anniversary of incorporation, or within 14 days after any register update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain registers or confirm UBO details may result in a fine not exceeding USD 5,000 and potential liability of the registered agent; persistent failure can support strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory audit for an exempt International Company that does not carry on business in Samoa, holds no Samoan real property, and is not listed; audit is required only if the company elects to have its financial statements audited or if a shareholder holding at least 10% of voting rights requests an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS if financial statements are voluntarily prepared and audited; simplified cash-basis or local GAAP acceptable for internal records of an exempt International Company.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual confirmation to the licensed registered agent must verify current beneficial owners and any shareholding transfers, changes in control, or changes to directors and officers. The UBO register is kept at the registered office and is not open to public inspection. Any transfer of shares must be recorded in the Register of Members, and the registered agent must be notified within 14 days after the transfer.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - 1,200 per annum for licensed registered agent and registered office services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 - 3,500 for a certified audit if voluntarily required or shareholder-requested

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 0% for International Companies (ICs). The International Companies Act 1987, s.198, grants a permanent statutory exemption from all Samoan income tax, capital gains tax, stamp duties, and withholding taxes in exchange for a fixed annual government license fee. Separate incentives for resident approved enterprises under the Investment Promotion Act 2021 may provide income tax holidays of up to five years; however, the standard offshore IC relies on the absolute statutory exemption and files no corporate income tax return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Return of an International Company (Form IC-AR); lodged through the licensed registered agent's portal with the Registrar of International and Foreign Companies under the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour; the annual government license fee is settled simultaneously.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within three months after each anniversary date of incorporation; the annual fee payment is due on the incorporation anniversary date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered name, International Company number, date of incorporation, registered office in Samoa, and registered agent identity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders are permitted; provide the registered agent address as the Samoan service-of-process address.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of authorized capital that determines the tiered annual license fee band.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Fee bands: USD 100 for capital up to USD 10,000; USD 400 for USD 10,001 to USD 1,000,000; USD 1,000 above USD 1,000,000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full names, residential or business addresses, and nationality of each director and the company secretary.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors are lawful; the registered agent or a resident secretary must remain contactable in Samoa.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ultimate individual beneficial owner details, shareholding percentage, and maintenance of the internal beneficial ownership register.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Details are confidential and non-public; nominee custodian entries are acceptable if the underlying declaration is retained by the registered agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of whether the IC carries on any relevant activity in Samoa and whether it claims Samoan or foreign tax residence.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a remote no-code website builder collecting SaaS subscription revenue via Stripe and Paddle, declare no relevant activity in Samoa and document genuine foreign management or tax residence to avoid shell-company characterization.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual return triggers a surcharge of 10% of the annual fee per month or part-month; continued default beyond six months exposes the IC to administrative strike-off and dissolution, with assets vesting in the State unless restoration is obtained by court order.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Samoa Revenue Authority Company Income Tax Return (Form IR-C1); e-filed through the SRA 'eTax Samoa' online portal by a registered tax agent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within three months after the end of the income year, which is the calendar year unless a substituted year is approved; therefore generally due by 31 March. Provisional tax installments are paid quarterly.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Worldwide assessable income derived; SaaS and low-code platform subscription revenue is reportable on an invoiced gross basis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents report only Samoan-source income; export of software services by a non-resident with no Samoan permanent establishment is not Samoan-source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ordinary operating expenses under the Income Tax Act 2015, including software development costs, hosting fees, and payment processor charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions are allowed only against assessable income; non-residents without assessable Samoan income file nil returns only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Items excluded from assessable income, including dividends from exempt International Companies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident IC relying on the s.198 exemption cites the International Companies Act and discloses no taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final liability computed by applying 27% to taxable income after deductions and offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Nil for an exempt IC; a taxed resident branch would compute 27% on Samoan-source profits attributable to a permanent establishment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a fixed penalty of SAT 500 plus 2% of unpaid tax per month; late payment interest accrues at the statutory rate; fraudulent evasion is punishable by penalty up to 100% of the tax evaded and imprisonment of up to three years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for International Companies: dividends and other profit distributions paid by a Samoan IC are statutorily exempt from withholding tax under s.198 of the International Companies Act 1987. For taxed resident companies, the domestic final withholding tax on dividends paid to non-residents is 15%; applicable DTA rates may reduce this to 5% or 15% depending on shareholding thresholds.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Samoa's DTA network is limited, comprising conventions with China and New Zealand (in-force status of any inherited or later agreement must be verified). To invoke treaty relief: (i) obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence from the foreign revenue authority; (ii) submit the SRA 'Application for Treaty Relief - Withholding Tax' form and the original TRC before payment is made; (iii) append a beneficial ownership statement and supporting transactional documents; (iv) expect denial of treaty benefits where a Samoan IC claims residence without economic substance or fails the beneficial-owner test. Professional advice is mandatory because an exempt IC typically self-characterizes as a non-resident company for treaty purposes.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 15% final withholding tax on outbound royalties paid for software and intellectual property, and 15% on outbound interest. Treaty rates generally reduce royalties and interest to between 10% and 15%, with interest eligible for a 10% rate in certain conventions. For an IC payor, the statutory exemption reduces both rates to 0% when the payments are genuine subscription revenue from the no-code SaaS platform and not disguised distributions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A transfer pricing documentation obligation in the form of a Local File, and a Master File where the group exceeds the reporting threshold, arises when the aggregate value of cross-border related-party transactions exceeds SAT 250,000 (approximately USD 94,000) in an income year. Country-by-Country reporting applies to groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa applies the OECD Forum on Harmful Tax Practices substance standard: an IC claiming the statutory tax exemption must demonstrate management and control in Samoa, adequate physical presence, employee capacity, and local expenditure proportionate to its core income-generating activities (CIGA), or must establish genuine foreign tax residence. Pure intellectual-property holding and conduit licensing arrangements are rebutted under the modified nexus approach; accordingly, the target no-code website builder monetizing via Stripe and Paddle must maintain either real Samoan substance or a verifiable foreign tax residence to remain defensible.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the exempt IC as a bare invoice mill that collects Stripe and Paddle SaaS subscription revenues while management, development personnel, and bank accounts are located in a mainland residence jurisdiction, with no board control exercised in Samoa.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of undeclared Samoan-source income on a permanent-establishment basis; 100% evasion penalty; late payment interest; strike-off of the company; criminal fine up to SAT 100,000; confiscation of misapplied subscription funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and shadow directors are jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax and civil restitution; the Samoa Revenue Authority may issue departure prohibition orders (travel bans) against directors pending settlement, and convicted individuals face imprisonment of up to three years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Beneficial Ownership Breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the annual return and beneficial ownership schedule; use of undisclosed nominee shareholders while concealing the ultimate Chinese family-trust principals; refusal to identify the beneficial owner on the register.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Accrual of the 10% monthly late-fee surcharge; administrative strike-off and dissolution of the IC without a court restoration order; fines for beneficial-ownership register violations; refusal of certificate of good standing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors attract personal fines, disqualification from managing any Samoan company, and joint and several liability to creditors; nominee directors who conceal the principal are personally liable for resultant damages and may be criminally prosecuted.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing subscription payments through Stripe or Paddle while transacting with OFAC, EU, or UN-sanctioned persons; failing to submit suspicious transaction reports under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018; handling proceeds connected to organized crime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to SAT 1,000,000; revocation of the licensed registered agent's authorization; freezing of balances held in Samoan banks; seizure of platform assets; exclusion from international payment rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal criminal liability and imprisonment of up to seven years for money-laundering facilitation; travel bans and asset freezes may be imposed, with extradition exposure to foreign enforcement authorities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Profit Repatriation Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Invoicing supra-normal royalties or management fees from the low-code platform to a related low-tax distribution entity; distributing subscription profits as undocumented 'dividends' or through circular intercompany loans to avoid arm's-length consideration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Arm's-length recharacterization; disallowance of excessive deductions; additional tax at 27%; penalty equal to 50% to 100% of the understated tax; statutory interest from the original due date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors approving non-commercial intercompany arrangements bear civil restitution liability for the shortfall; artificial pricing schemes expose them to fraudulent-evasion prosecution and personal asset seizure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Declaring 'no relevant activity in Samoa' while continuing to claim IC tax exemption; absence of records demonstrating where the SaaS platform is managed; failure to file the economic substance declaration or to rectify residence status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Retroactive revocation of the s.198 exemption; reassessment of all income at 27%; penalties up to SAT 500,000; mandatory removal from the International Companies Register with loss of legal personality.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors incur joint and several liability for the reassessed tax and penalties; disqualification orders and departure bans are available to compel settlement of the company's tax debts.
